title: Launch and inspect an EC2 instance

screens.title: Find EC2 and check the Region
screens.action: Confirm account and Region. Open Instances, then choose Launch instances.
screens.why: Resources are created in the selected account and Region.

screens.title: Name the instance and choose an AMI
screens.path: EC2 → Instances → Launch instances → Name and tags / Application and OS Images
screens.action: Enter architect-console-lab and choose the Amazon Linux 2023 AMI.
screens.why: Name is a tag; the AMI selects OS, publisher and architecture.
rows: Application and OS Images (Amazon Machine Image)

screens.title: Choose instance type and key pair
screens.path: Launch an instance → Instance type / Key pair (login)
screens.action: Choose an available small instance type and select/create a lab key pair.
screens.why: Instance type sets capacity; the private key must be downloaded and stored safely.
screens.warning: Instance pricing and Free Tier eligibility vary by account, Region and date. Verify the current estimate in your own console.

screens.title: Edit VPC and subnet settings
screens.path: Launch an instance → Network settings → Edit
screens.action: Choose a lab VPC, public subnet and enable public IPv4 for this connection exercise.
screens.why: A public subnet needs an internet gateway route, and the instance needs a public address.
rows: Public subnet with internet gateway route

screens.title: Scope the security group
screens.path: Launch an instance → Network settings → Firewall (security groups)
screens.action: Use a lab security group with SSH TCP 22 allowed only from My IP.
screens.why: Do not use Anywhere for SSH. The actual source must match your public IP.
screens.warning: A new security group may default SSH to Anywhere (0.0.0.0/0). Choose My IP for this exercise before launching.

screens.title: Review storage and launch
screens.path: Launch an instance → Configure storage → Summary
screens.action: Review gp3 root volume, delete-on-termination, all summary choices and estimated cost; choose Launch instance.
screens.why: The right Summary panel is the final review before resources can incur charges.

screens.title: Inspect status and resource details
screens.path: EC2 → Instances → Select instance → Details / Security / Storage / Monitoring
screens.action: Open the instance ID. Check running, 2/2 status checks, public/private IP, security group and EBS volume.
screens.why: Running alone does not prove guest health or network reachability.
rows: Root EBS gp3 · delete on termination

screens.title: Connect and check the guest
screens.path: EC2 → Instances → Select instance → Connect → EC2 Instance Connect
screens.action: Choose EC2 Instance Connect, confirm the user, then run whoami and uptime in the browser session.
screens.why: Connection requires a supported image, permissions and a reachable network path.

screens.title: Terminate and verify cleanup
screens.path: EC2 → Instances → Instance state → Terminate (delete) instance
screens.action: Confirm Terminate (delete), monitor Shutting-down, then review volumes, snapshots, key pair and IP allocations.
screens.why: Termination is permanent; some separately created resources can remain billable.

title: Create a service role and inspect permissions

screens.title: Open Roles
screens.action: Open Roles, inspect existing roles, then choose Create role.
screens.why: An IAM role is an assumed identity with its own trust and permission policies.

screens.title: Select trusted entity
screens.action: Choose AWS service, select EC2 under Service or use case, then choose Next.
screens.why: This creates the trust relationship that lets EC2 assume the role.

screens.title: Define scoped policy
screens.path: Add permissions → Create policy → Specify permissions
screens.action: Open Create policy in a new tab. Choose JSON; allow s3:GetObject only on arn:aws:s3:::architect-lab-bucket/examples/*, then choose Next.
screens.why: The action and object ARN scope limit what the role can read. Replace the example bucket with your approved lab bucket.
screens.warning: Use an approved bucket that you own. A bucket policy or explicit deny can still block access.

screens.title: Create the policy
screens.action: Name the customer managed policy LabS3ReadObjects, review its action and resource, then choose Create policy. Return to the role wizard tab.
screens.why: The policy has to exist before it can be selected in the role wizard.

screens.title: Attach permissions
screens.action: Refresh the policy list if necessary, search LabS3ReadObjects, select its checkbox, and choose Next.
screens.why: The attached permissions policy controls actions after EC2 assumes the role.

screens.title: Name and create role
screens.path: Create role → Name, review, and create
screens.action: Enter ec2-lab-s3-read, verify the EC2 trusted entity and LabS3ReadObjects policy, then choose Create role.
screens.why: Review trust and permissions together before creating an account-wide identity.

screens.title: Verify trust relationship
screens.action: Open the created role. In Trust relationships, verify ec2.amazonaws.com and sts:AssumeRole; in Permissions, confirm the attached policy. Delete the role and policy after the lab.
screens.why: A policy attachment alone does not prove the trust path or resource policy permits access.

title: Build and trace a public subnet

screens.title: Create the VPC
screens.action: Choose VPC only, name lab-vpc, and select a non-overlapping IPv4 CIDR.
screens.why: CIDR overlap limits future connectivity.

screens.title: Create a subnet
screens.action: Choose lab-vpc, one Availability Zone and 10.20.1.0/24.
screens.why: Subnets live in one Availability Zone and inherit VPC address space.

screens.title: Attach gateway and route
screens.path: VPC → Internet gateways → Create / Attach → Route tables → Edit routes
screens.action: Attach an internet gateway and add 0.0.0.0/0 to it in a dedicated route table.
screens.why: A subnet becomes public by its effective route to an internet gateway.

screens.title: Associate and verify
screens.path: Route tables → Subnet associations → Edit associations
screens.action: Associate the lab subnet; inspect effective routes and security controls, then remove lab resources in dependency order.
screens.why: Creating a route table is insufficient until the subnet uses it.

title: Create and secure an S3 bucket

screens.title: Open bucket creation
screens.path: S3 → General purpose buckets → Create bucket
screens.action: Choose a globally unique lab bucket name and an approved Region.
screens.why: Bucket identity and Region affect naming and data location.

screens.title: Keep public access blocked
screens.path: Create bucket → Object Ownership → Block Public Access
screens.action: Keep bucket owner enforced and all Block Public Access settings enabled.
screens.why: A private lab bucket needs no public ACL or policy.

screens.title: Choose protection settings
screens.path: Create bucket → Bucket Versioning → Default encryption
screens.action: Enable versioning for this exercise; review default SSE-S3 encryption.
screens.why: Versioning helps recover prior versions; encryption and lifecycle are separate controls.

screens.title: Inspect and clean up
screens.action: Upload a harmless test file; inspect version ID and access; delete object versions, then bucket.
screens.why: Versioned buckets must be emptied of all versions and delete markers before deletion.

screens.title: Choose database engine
screens.action: Select Standard create and an approved engine/version for a disposable lab.
screens.why: Standard create exposes networking, storage, backup and availability choices.

screens.title: Set instance and credentials
screens.path: Create database → Settings / Instance configuration / Storage
screens.action: Name the DB, select a small class and storage, and use approved credential management.
screens.why: Class and storage influence capacity and cost; never put real passwords into a training site.

screens.title: Set private connectivity
screens.action: Choose VPC, DB subnet group, public access No, and a narrow application security group.
screens.why: A private DB needs app-to-DB reachability, not public exposure.
rows: Private subnets in at least two Availability Zones
Allow app SG on DB port

screens.title: Inspect and delete
screens.path: RDS → Databases → Connectivity & security / Monitoring / Maintenance
screens.action: Inspect endpoint, port, backup and metrics; delete the disposable DB and review final snapshot choice.
screens.why: Database deletion and snapshots have lasting data and cost consequences.

title: Create and observe a Lambda function

screens.title: Create from scratch
screens.action: Choose Author from scratch, name the function, and select a supported runtime.
screens.why: Runtime, architecture and execution role govern compatibility and permissions.

screens.title: Review execution role
screens.path: Create function → Change default execution role
screens.action: Use a lab role with basic log permissions and inspect its IAM policy.
screens.why: The execution role is the function's AWS identity, distinct from who invokes it.

screens.title: Deploy and test
screens.action: Deploy a simple handler, create a harmless test event and invoke once.
screens.why: A successful deployment does not prove an invocation succeeds.

screens.title: Inspect evidence and clean up
screens.path: Function → Monitor → View CloudWatch logs / Configuration
screens.action: Inspect result, duration, errors and logs; delete function and lab log group/role if appropriate.
screens.why: Logs and roles can remain after a function is deleted.

title: Inspect a metric and create an alarm

screens.title: Find the metric
screens.action: Choose the namespace, dimensions and metric for a lab resource.
screens.why: Metric dimensions identify the exact resource being monitored.

screens.title: Define alarm conditions
screens.action: Review period, statistic, threshold and missing-data treatment.
screens.why: A threshold without a period or missing-data policy is ambiguous.

screens.title: Choose actions
screens.path: Create alarm → Notification / Name and description
screens.action: Choose an approved SNS topic or no action for practice; name the alarm.
screens.why: Alarm evaluation and notification delivery are separate.

screens.title: Inspect state and cleanup
screens.path: CloudWatch → Alarms → All alarms → Alarm details
screens.action: Inspect history, state and graph; delete the lab alarm, and unsubscribe lab notifications if created.
screens.why: An OK state may reflect no recent breach, not necessarily that collection is healthy.

title: Trace a DNS record to its target

screens.title: Find hosted zone
screens.action: Open an existing authorized lab hosted zone; do not register a new domain for this exercise.
screens.why: A hosted zone is the authoritative DNS record container when delegation is correct.

screens.title: Create record
screens.action: Use a lab name, A/alias or CNAME as appropriate, and a controlled target.
screens.why: Alias choice and target type depend on the AWS resource.

screens.title: Review routing
screens.path: Create record → Routing policy / Evaluate target health
screens.action: Use Simple routing for a single target and review TTL/health options.
screens.why: Routing policy changes how clients receive answers.

screens.title: Test and cleanup
screens.action: Test expected answer and inspect target health; remove only the lab record.
screens.why: A record can exist without public delegation or a healthy target.

screens.title: Find the attached group
screens.action: Open the group attached to the lab instance.
screens.why: Rules only apply when the group is associated with a network interface.

screens.title: Inspect inbound rules
screens.action: Check protocol, port and source before editing.
screens.why: An open port without the right source or route may still be unreachable.

screens.title: Make a narrow change
screens.path: Inbound rules → Edit inbound rules → Save rules
screens.action: Add only the required source for the lab, then save.
screens.why: 0.0.0.0/0 exposes SSH to every IPv4 source.

screens.title: Verify and restore
screens.path: Security group details → Inbound rules / Outbound rules
screens.action: Test the intended connection and remove temporary access.
screens.why: Confirm the effective rule and recheck the original symptom.

title: Attach a volume and take a snapshot

screens.title: Find volumes
screens.action: Inspect volume type, size, encryption, state and Availability Zone.
screens.why: An EBS volume must attach to an instance in the same Availability Zone.

screens.title: Create a test volume
screens.action: Choose gp3, small capacity, encryption and matching AZ.
screens.why: Storage can incur charges even if it is not attached.

screens.title: Attach and verify
screens.action: Choose the lab instance; inspect attachment state and guest device.
screens.why: AWS attachment alone does not format or mount a filesystem.

screens.title: Snapshot and clean up
screens.action: Verify snapshot state; detach/delete test volume and remove test snapshot.
screens.why: Snapshot and unattached volume charges can remain.

title: Create an ALB and inspect target health

screens.title: Choose load balancer
screens.path: EC2 → Load Balancers → Create load balancer
screens.action: Select Application Load Balancer and an approved scheme.
screens.why: Internet-facing and internal schemes define different entry points.

screens.title: Choose network and access
screens.path: Create ALB → Network mapping / Security groups
screens.action: Choose VPC, two suitable AZ subnets and an ALB security group.
screens.why: A public ALB needs supported subnets and inbound listener access.

screens.title: Connect listener to target group
screens.path: Listeners and routing → Create target group
screens.action: Select instance target type, application port and health check path.
screens.why: A listener forwards only to targets that pass health checks.

screens.title: Inspect health and cleanup
screens.path: EC2 → Target Groups → Targets / Health checks
screens.action: Check target state and reason; remove ALB, target group and lab rules.
screens.why: A running instance can be unhealthy behind the load balancer.

title: Create a table and inspect an item

screens.title: Create table
screens.action: Name a lab table and choose partition key; add sort key only if needed.
screens.why: Primary key design shapes access patterns.

screens.title: Choose capacity and protection
screens.action: Review on-demand/provisioned mode, encryption and point-in-time recovery.
screens.why: Capacity mode and recovery settings affect operation and cost.

screens.title: Write and find an item
screens.path: Table → Explore table items → Create item
screens.action: Insert a harmless item; compare Get item or Query with Scan.
screens.why: Query uses a key; Scan reads across the table.

screens.title: Inspect and delete
screens.action: Inspect status and metrics; delete test item/table and any backup.
screens.why: Deletion choices can leave backups or exports.

title: Trace an API action in event history

screens.title: Open event history
screens.action: Check Region and time range before filtering.
screens.why: Event history is a lookup view; coverage and retention differ from a trail or event data store.

screens.title: Find the caller
screens.action: Filter by event name or resource and open the event.
screens.why: The displayed user identity may be an assumed role.

screens.title: Read the event JSON
screens.action: Inspect userIdentity, eventSource, eventName, resources and errorCode.
screens.why: The event establishes caller, action, target and result.

screens.title: Correlate and preserve
screens.path: Event history → Download events / trail configuration
screens.action: Correlate with EC2 state, then inspect trail settings for durable logging.
screens.why: A missing event in one Region/filter is not proof that no API call occurred.
rows: No resource created in this tour

title: Review a stack change and rollback

screens.title: Open stack
screens.action: Select a lab stack and inspect status, resources and outputs.
screens.why: Stack status alone does not describe every resource state.

screens.title: Prepare a change set
screens.path: Stack actions → Create change set for current stack
screens.action: Use a lab template update and name the change set.
screens.why: A change set previews proposed resource actions before execution.

screens.title: Review impact
screens.action: Read Add, Modify and Remove actions, replacement and drift risk.
screens.why: Replacement can recreate a stateful resource.

screens.title: Execute and verify
screens.action: Watch events, outputs and rollback; delete the lab stack when complete.
screens.why: A failed update can roll back; verify resulting resources.
rows: Delete lab stack and residual resources

screens.title: Inspect cluster
screens.action: Check infrastructure type, tasks and service inventory.
screens.why: A cluster organizes services; tasks run the containers.

screens.title: Define a task
screens.path: Task definitions → Create new task definition
screens.action: Review image URI, CPU/memory, execution role, task role and logs.
screens.why: Execution role pulls images; task role grants app AWS API access.

screens.title: Create service
screens.action: Choose task definition, desired count, subnets, SG and load balancer if required.
screens.why: Network and health checks determine successful deployment.

screens.title: Inspect deployment
screens.action: Read stopped task reasons, target health and logs; delete service and lab artifacts.
screens.why: A deployment can roll back despite a healthy cluster.

title: Trace a cost change to usage

screens.title: Open cost view
screens.path: Billing and Cost Management → Cost Explorer
screens.action: Choose a comparable time window and granularity.
screens.why: A total bill hides service and account drivers.

screens.title: Group the spend
screens.path: Cost Explorer → Cost and usage → Group by
screens.action: Group by service, then Region or usage type.
screens.why: The dominant service may contain several usage drivers.

screens.title: Find the usage driver
screens.action: Compare current and prior period; inspect data transfer and idle resources.
screens.why: A cost spike may come from usage, rates or commitment changes.

screens.title: Set follow-up
screens.action: Record owner and prevention; configure an approved budget or anomaly alert.
screens.why: Delayed billing data should be correlated with actual resource inventory.
